propositions: Pass-1 context-limit escalation silently relocates calls to direct Anthropic by discarding the run's provider qualifier, causing failures in provider-isolated containers or unbudgeted spend.
The _rung_target function derives escalation targets from module constants without considering the run's actual model, so it returns bare Anthropic ids even when the run is configured for Bedrock.
Entry rung uses 'frontier' which resolves to an Anthropic-qualified model, so models_at_or_above on the one-criterion retry path unwantedly substitutes to a bare model id before escalation is needed.
When a model-class table is unconfigured and cfg.model is provider-qualified, composing escalation targets as bare ids creates invalid model strings like 'bedrock:claude-opus-4-8'.

The fix threads the primary model into _rung_target and compares inferred providers: if providers differ on a higher rung, drop the rung instead of crossing providers; if on the primary's own rung, use the primary verbatim to preserve provider context.
